problem: Find the value of $c$ that satisfies the mean value theorem for $f(x)={log}_{2}⁡x$ on the interval $[4,16].$

feedback.worked_solution:
The function $f(x)$ is continuous on $[4,9]$ and differentiable on $(4,9),$ hence we can apply the mean value theorem. 

So, the mean value theorem states that there exists a $c\in (4,9)$ such that

$$
{f}^{′}(c)=\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}.
$$

Plugging in $a=4$ and $b=9$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(c) & =\frac{f(9)-f(4)}{9-4} \\  & =\frac{(5\sqrt{9}-2)-(5\sqrt{4}-2)}{5} \\  & =\frac{13-8}{5} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Differentiating the function, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5\sqrt{x}-2)=\frac{5}{2\sqrt{x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{f}^{′}(c)=\frac{5}{2\sqrt{c}}.
$$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2\sqrt{c}} & =1 \\ \sqrt{c} & =\frac{5}{2} \\ c & ={(\frac{5}{2})}^{2} \\ c & =\frac{25}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
